mainTopic: Sukkah 6b: חציצה and גזירה לגזירה; what the הלכה למשה מסיני of מחיצין teaches; how many walls a סוכה needs and where the one-טפח wall stands
overview: The amud opens in the middle of the גמרא's list of laws that are a הלכה למשה מסיני. It first defines a חציצה in טבילה: by Torah law, a blockage counts only if it covers most of the body and the person minds it. The Sages added two decrees, but not a third, because we do not make a גזירה לגזירה. Next, the גמרא asks what the הלכה למשה מסיני of מחיצין teaches according to רבי מאיר, who already learns the ten-טפחים height from פסוקים. The answer is that it teaches גוד, לבוד, and דופן עקומה. Then the גמרא turns to the משנה's rule that a סוכה needs walls. In a ברייתא, the רבנן require two full walls plus a טפח, and רבי שמעון requires three full walls plus a טפח. The גמרא gives four ways to explain this מחלוקת, and רב מתנה gives a separate source for רבי שמעון from a פסוק in ישעיה. Finally, רב rules where the one-טפח wall is placed, and רב כהנא and רב אסי begin to respond to him, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Torah-level rule of a blocking substance
steps.stepSummary: By Torah law, a blockage counts as a חציצה only if it covers most of the body and the person minds it being there.
steps.simpleTranslation: By Torah law, if the blockage covers the majority of the body and the person minds it, it blocks the immersion. If he does not mind it, it does not block.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the basic Torah-level definition of a חציצה: two conditions must both be present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two conditions are רובו (covers the majority of the body) and מקפיד (the person minds it and would want it removed). If either one is missing, the Torah does not consider the immersion blocked. In context, the גמרא says this to show that the other cases (a minority he minds, a majority he does not mind) are only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law (as opposed to rabbinic law)
Minds it, is bothered by it, and would want it removed
Blocks or interposes, so the immersion does not work

steps.confusionAlert: Both conditions are needed together at the Torah level. A small blockage that he minds does not block by Torah law. Neither does a large blockage he ignores. Each of those blocks only מדרבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This two-part test, רובו plus מקפיד, is the foundation of all הלכות חציצה in טבילה.

phrases.english: By Torah law,
if it covers the majority of his body and he minds it, it interposes;
phrases.notes: Both conditions must be present.

phrases.english: but if he does not mind it, it does not interpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה, רוּבּוֹ וּמַקְפִּיד עָלָיו — חוֹצֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (on the previous amud) about which details of חציצין are rabbinic and which are a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah-level חציצה requires both רובו and מקפיד.

steps.title: The two rabbinic decrees on blocking substances
steps.stepSummary: The Sages extended the rule with two decrees: a majority he does not mind, and a minority he does mind, both because they resemble a majority he minds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages decreed about a majority he does not mind, because of a majority he minds. They also decreed about a minority he minds, because of a majority he minds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists the two rabbinic extensions of the Torah rule. Each one is a protective fence around the Torah-level case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each decree keeps one of the two Torah conditions and drops the other. If you keep רובו and drop מקפיד, you get the first decree. If you keep מקפיד and drop רובו, you get the second. The Sages worried that people would confuse these near-identical cases with the real Torah case of רובו המקפיד.

keyTerms.meaning: A minority (small part) of his body
Because of, out of concern for

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why in practice we are careful about even small blockages a person minds, and about large ones he does not mind.

phrases.english: And they decreed regarding a majority that he does not mind
because of a majority that he minds,
and regarding a minority that he minds
because of a majority that he minds.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְגָזְרוּ עַל רוּבּוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַקְפִּיד מִשּׁוּם רוּבּוֹ הַמַּקְפִּיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds rabbinic layers on top of the Torah rule from Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rabbinically, both רובו שאינו מקפיד and מיעוטו המקפיד are treated as חציצה.

steps.title: Why not also decree on a small blockage he does not mind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why not also decree on a minority he does not mind, since it resembles the cases that were already decreed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let them also decree on a minority he does not mind, because of a minority he minds, or alternatively because of a majority he does not mind!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the list of decrees. It asks why the fourth possible case was left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one of the four combinations is still permitted: a small blockage that he does not mind. This last case looks like each of the two decreed cases, so the גמרא asks why it was not decreed as well. The question assumes that resemblance alone is enough reason to make a decree.

phrases.aramaic: וְלִיגְזַר נָמֵי עַל מִיעוּטוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַקְפִּיד
phrases.english: Then let them also decree regarding a minority he does not mind
because of a minority that he minds,

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי מִשּׁוּם רוּבּוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַקְפִּיד!
phrases.english: or alternatively, because of a majority that he does not mind!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיגְזַר נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the completeness of the decrees listed in Step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision to decree on only two of the three non-Torah cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A minority he does not mind looks like the cases already decreed, so it should be included too.

steps.title: No decree to protect another decree
steps.stepSummary: Those cases are themselves decrees, and we do not make a decree on top of a decree (גזירה לגזירה).
steps.simpleTranslation: That case itself is only a decree. Should we then go and make a decree to protect a decree?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the cases the fourth one resembles are already only rabbinic decrees, so there is no reason to add another layer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A decree is meant to protect a Torah law. The fourth case resembles only the two decreed cases, not the Torah case of רובו המקפיד. Decreeing it would mean a fence around a fence, which the Sages do not do.

keyTerms.meaning: A decree to protect another decree, which is generally not done

steps.whatToRemember: Torah law requires רובו plus מקפיד. The Sages added two decrees, each missing one condition. The case missing both conditions is permitted, because we do not make a גזירה לגזירה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle of גזירה לגזירה (no decree upon a decree) appears throughout ש"ס as a limit on rabbinic extensions.

phrases.english: That itself is a decree,
and shall we arise and decree
a decree to protect a decree?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הִיא גּוּפָא גְּזֵירָה, וַאֲנַן נֵיקוּם וְנִגְזֹר גְּזֵירָה לִגְזֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any case resembling a decreed case should also be decreed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Decrees protect only Torah law; we do not make a גזירה לגזירה.

steps.title: Partitions: as already explained
steps.stepSummary: The next item on the list, מחיצין, is the ten-טפחים height of partitions that was discussed earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: Partitions: that is what we said earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next הלכה למשה מסיני on the list, partitions. It points back to an earlier discussion and is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא said that the minimum height of ten טפחים for a מחיצה is a הלכה למשה מסיני according to רבי יהודה. Here it simply refers back to that discussion instead of repeating it.

phrases.english: Partitions: that which we stated earlier.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְחִיצִין — הָא דַּאֲמַרַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from חציצין to the next item on the list of הלכות למשה מסיני.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ten-טפחים height of a מחיצה is a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: What does the partition tradition teach according to רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The tradition works for רבי יהודה, but רבי מאיר derives ten טפחים from the פסוקים, so what is the הלכה למשה מסיני needed for?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבי יהודה. But according to רבי מאיר, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim from Step 5. For רבי מאיר, the ten-טפחים height already comes from the פסוקים, so a tradition from Sinai would seem unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that all אמות in the משכן measure six טפחים, so the ארון plus the כפורת add up to ten טפחים, learned from the פסוקים. רבי יהודה cannot derive it that way, so for him the tradition is necessary. The question is what the הלכה למשה מסיני of מחיצין adds for רבי מאיר; the answer comes next.

phrases.english: This works well according to Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר — מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?
phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Meir, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר — מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how Step 5 fits with רבי מאיר's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מחיצין is a הלכה למשה מסיני, according to רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר learns ten טפחים from the פסוקים, so the tradition seems to have nothing to teach.

steps.title: The tradition teaches other partition rules
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי מאיר, the הלכה למשה מסיני comes to teach גוד, לבוד, and דופן עקומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the הלכה came, it came to teach גוד, לבוד, and דופן עקומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6. Even for רבי מאיר, the הלכה למשה מסיני has a job: it teaches three special rules about partitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר learns the ten-טפחים height from the פסוקים, so the tradition is not needed for that. Instead, the tradition teaches three rules that let a partition count even when it is not a complete, solid wall. These rules cannot be found in the Torah's text, so only a tradition from סיני could teach them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Extend': a partition is treated as if it continues up or down to fill a missing height
'Joined': a gap of less than three טְפָחִים is treated as closed
'Bent wall': invalid roofing of up to four אַמּוֹת next to a wall counts as if the wall bends over
The הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי (oral tradition given to משה at סיני)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי מאיר, ten טפחים comes from the פסוקים. The הלכה למשה מסיני teaches גוד, לבוד, and דופן עקומה.

phrases.english: When the halacha [from Sinai] came,
phrases.notes: It came to teach the following:

phrases.english: it was for 'extending,' 'joining,' and a 'bent wall.'
phrases.notes: Three ways a partition counts even though it is not a full, solid wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתַאי הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the tradition a different job: it teaches other partition rules
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבי מאיר, the הלכה למשה מסיני about partitions would have nothing left to teach
steps.terutzMaskana: The tradition teaches גוד, לבוד, and דופן עקומה, which are not written in the Torah

steps.title: Next case in the משנה: a סוכה without three walls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה: a סוכה that does not have three walls is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] And one that does not have three walls [is invalid].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new topic. It quotes the next line of the משנה so that it can discuss it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a heading (דיבור המתחיל). It sets up the discussion of how many walls a סוכה needs. The next step brings a ברייתא with the details.

phrases.english: And one that does not have three walls.
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה: such a סוכה is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁאֵין לָהּ שָׁלֹשׁ דְּפָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the next case from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה without three walls is invalid

steps.title: How many full walls a סוכה needs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the רבנן require two full walls plus a third of one טפח. רבי שמעון requires three full walls plus a fourth of one טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: two walls must be full walls, and the third can be even one טפח. רבי שמעון says: three must be full walls, and the fourth can be even one טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with an argument over exactly how many walls a סוכה needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the last wall only needs to be one טפח wide. They argue about how many walls before it must be complete. The רבנן require three walls in total (two full walls and one small one). רבי שמעון requires four walls in total (three full walls and one small one).

keyTerms.meaning: 'According to their law': full, complete walls
A תַּנָּא who disagrees with the רבנן here

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not mean that a סוכה needs four full walls. Only three must be full; the fourth only needs to be one טפח.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Two [walls must be] in their proper form,
phrases.notes: Full walls.

phrases.english: and the third, even one handbreadth.
Rabbi Shimon says:
Three [walls must be] in their proper form,
and the fourth, even one handbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that explains the משנה's rule about walls
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבנן: two full walls plus a third of one טפח. רבי שמעון: three full walls plus a fourth of one טפח.

steps.title: What is the root of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle the רבנן and רבי שמעון disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the argument. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is not challenging either side. It wants to know what underlying idea causes them to reach different numbers of walls.

keyTerms.meaning: 'About what do they disagree?': asks for the root of a dispute

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the dispute in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that explains why the רבנן and רבי שמעון disagree

steps.title: Spelling versus reading of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold יש אם למסורת: we learn from how the word is spelled. רבי שמעון holds יש אם למקרא: we learn from how the word is read aloud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold that the written spelling is the main source. רבי שמעון holds that the way it is read is the main source.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: they disagree about how to learn from the Torah's words. One side follows the spelling, and the other side follows the pronunciation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word סוכות appears in the פסוקים about the סוכה. Sometimes it is spelled without a ו, so in writing it can look singular, but it is read aloud as plural. If you count the walls from the spelling, you get fewer walls (the רבנן). If you count from the pronunciation, you get more walls (רבי שמעון). The גמרא will show the exact count next.

keyTerms.meaning: The written spelling of the Torah is the main source for learning
The way the Torah is read aloud is the main source for learning

steps.whyThisMatters: מסורת versus מקרא is a general rule for learning from פסוקים, and it comes up in many places across ש״ס.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
the written tradition [spelling] is authoritative,
and Rabbi Shimon holds:
the reading [vocalization] is authoritative.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: יֵשׁ אֵם לַמָּסוֹרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה in step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן follow the spelling (מסורת), and רבי שמעון follows the reading (מקרא) of the word סוכות in the פסוקים

steps.title: The math of the רבנן: four mentions become three walls
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן follow the spelling. Two singular words plus one plural word give four. One is used for the מצוה itself, which leaves three walls. The הלכה למשה מסיני reduces the third wall to one טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold that the spelling counts. The תורה writes בסכת (singular), בסכת (singular), and בסוכות (plural), which makes four. Take away one for the מצוה itself, and three are left. Two walls are full walls. Then the הלכה למשה מסיני comes, cuts down the third wall, and sets it at one טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows step by step how the רבנן get 'two walls plus a טפח' out of the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By spelling, two of the words have no ו, so each counts as one סוכה. The third has a ו, so it is plural, and a plural counts as two: 1+1+2=4. One mention is set aside to teach the מצוה of סוכה itself. The remaining three teach three walls, and the הלכה למשה מסיני lowers the third wall to just a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: For itself, meaning the basic מצוה of סוכה
In their normal, full form (full walls)

steps.confusionAlert: A plural word counts as TWO, because the smallest plural is two. That is why three words can add up to four (or six) סוכות.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold: the written spelling is authoritative,
phrases.notes: Picks up the principle from Step 11.

phrases.english: 'b'sukkat,' 'b'sukkat,' 'basukkot'
phrases.notes: Two are written without a ו (singular) and one with a ו (plural).

phrases.english: so here there are four.
Take away one for the מצוה itself,
and three are left.
phrases.notes: Three walls.

phrases.english: Two are full, normal walls,
and the halacha (from Sinai) came and reduced the third
phrases.notes: The הלכה למשה מסיני.

phrases.english: and set it at one handbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: יֵשׁ אֵם לַמָּסוֹרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the answer of Step 11 by showing the actual counting for the רבנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: By spelling there are 4 mentions. Minus 1 for the מצוה leaves 3 walls, and the third is reduced to a טפח.

steps.title: The math of רבי שמעון: six mentions become four walls
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון follows how the words are read. All three are read as plural, so the count is six. One word (worth two) is set aside for the מצוה, which leaves four walls. The הלכה reduces the fourth wall to a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון holds that the way the word is read counts. It is read בסוכות, בסוכות, בסוכות, which makes six. Take away one word of the פסוק for the מצוה itself, and four are left. Three walls are full walls. Then the הלכה למשה מסיני comes, cuts down the fourth wall, and sets it at one טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows the same counting for רבי שמעון, which explains why he requires three full walls plus a טפח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read aloud, all three words are plural, so each counts as two: 2+2+2=6. He subtracts one whole word (worth two) for the מצוה itself, which leaves four walls. Three are full walls, and the הלכה למשה מסיני lowers the fourth to a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: A verse / a word of the פסוק

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר: יֵשׁ אֵם לַמִּקְרָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon holds: the way it is read is authoritative,
'basukkot,' 'basukkot,' 'basukkot'
phrases.notes: All three are read as plural.

phrases.english: so here there are six,
take away one verse-word for the מצוה itself,
phrases.notes: One plural word, worth two.

phrases.english: and four are left.
Three are full, normal walls,
the halacha came and reduced the fourth
and set it at one handbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר: יֵשׁ אֵם לַמִּקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to Step 12, giving רבי שמעון's side of the counting.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: By reading there are 6 mentions. Minus one word (2) for the מצוה leaves 4 walls, and the fourth is reduced to a טפח.
steps.whatToRemember: Spelling (מסורת) gives 4, so the רבנן require 2 walls plus a טפח. Reading (מקרא) gives 6, so רבי שמעון requires 3 walls plus a טפח.

steps.title: A second explanation: does the roofing need its own verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another way to explain the מחלוקת. Both sides count by reading (6). They disagree about whether the סכך needs a פסוק of its own. The רבנן say it does, so one more mention is used up and only 3 walls remain. רבי שמעון says it does not, so 4 walls remain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: everyone agrees that the way it is read counts. Here they disagree about this: one master holds that the roofing needs a verse, and the other master holds that the roofing does not need a verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an alternative answer to the question of Step 10, moving the argument to a completely different issue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both sides start from six. The רבנן use up a mention for the מצוה itself and also one for the סכך, so only three walls are left (two full walls plus a טפח). רבי שמעון holds that the סכך is the essence of a סוכה and needs no extra source, so four walls are left (three full walls plus a טפח).

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead (introduces an alternative answer)

steps.confusionAlert: The two 'מר סבר' lines are not named. The first is the רבנן (the סכך needs a פסוק) and the second is רבי שמעון (it does not).
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the מחלוקת: (1) spelling vs. reading, or (2) everyone follows reading, and they argue whether the סכך needs its own פסוק.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
everyone agrees that the way it is read is authoritative,
phrases.notes: So both start with six.

phrases.english: and here this is what they disagree about:
one master holds: its roofing requires a verse,
phrases.notes: The רבנן: a mention is used for the סכך, so only 3 walls remain.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: סְכָכָה לָא בָּעֲיָא קְרָא.
phrases.english: and the other master holds: its roofing does not require a verse.
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון: 4 walls remain.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא יֵשׁ אֵם לַמִּקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to Step 10's question, instead of the spelling-vs-reading answer of Steps 11-13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Everyone follows יש אם למקרא. The argument is whether סכך needs its own פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same practical מחלוקת can come from a disagreement about how to read the text or from a disagreement about what a סוכה essentially is.

steps.title: Both follow the spelling; they disagree whether the הלכה takes away or adds
steps.stepSummary: Everyone holds יש אם למסורת, so the פסוקים yield three walls. The רבנן say the הלכה shrinks the third wall to a טפח. רבי שמעון says the הלכה adds a fourth wall of a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: everyone agrees that we follow the spelling. Here is what they really argue about. One side says the הלכה comes to take away. The other side says the הלכה comes to add.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third way to explain the מחלוקת. Now both sides count the same way, by spelling, and they argue about what the הלכה למשה מסיני does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By spelling, the count is four mentions. One is used for the מצוה itself, so three walls remain for both sides. The רבנן say the הלכה shrinks the third wall down to a טפח, which leaves 2 full walls and a טפח. רבי שמעון says the הלכה adds a fourth wall that only needs to be a טפח, which leaves 3 full walls and a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say: introduces another possible explanation
The הלכה, here meaning the הלכה למשה מסיני about walls

steps.confusionAlert: In this version, both sides start from the same three walls. The whole argument is about whether the טפח-wall replaces the third wall or is an extra fourth wall.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
that everyone agrees we follow the spelling,
and here they disagree about this:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: כִּי אֲתַאי הִלְכְתָא — לְגָרֵעַ.
phrases.english: One Sage holds: when the הלכה comes, it is to take away.
phrases.notes: The רבנן: the third wall is reduced to a טפח.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: כִּי אֲתַאי הִלְכְתָא — לְהוֹסִיף.
phrases.english: And the other Sage holds: when the הלכה comes, it is to add.
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון: a fourth wall of a טפח is added.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא יֵשׁ אֵם לַמָּסוֹרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third explanation of the same מחלוקת, after the explanations in steps 11-14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the root of the מחלוקת between the רבנן and רבי שמעון?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both follow the spelling. They disagree whether the הלכה למשה מסיני reduces a wall or adds one.

steps.title: They disagree whether the first mention of the word is counted
steps.stepSummary: Everyone holds יש אם למסורת and that the הלכה reduces. The argument is about דורשין תחילות. רבי שמעון counts the first mention, so he gets four walls. The רבנן do not count it, so they get three walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: everyone agrees the הלכה comes to take away, and everyone agrees we follow the spelling. Here they argue about whether we learn from the first mention. One side says we do learn from the first mention. The other side says we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a fourth way to explain the מחלוקת. Both sides now agree on the spelling and on what the הלכה does. The only question is whether the first mention of סוכה is counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spelling gives four mentions. If we count the first mention too (דורשין תחילות), we get four walls, and the הלכה shrinks the fourth wall to a טפח. That is רבי שמעון. If the first mention is only there to teach the מצוה itself (אין דורשין תחילות), we get three walls, and the הלכה shrinks the third wall to a טפח. That is the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn from the first mention too. The first time the word appears is also counted.
We do not learn from the first mention. It is needed for the basic מצוה and is not counted.

steps.whatToRemember: There are four explanations of the מחלוקת: (1) spelling versus reading; (2) whether the סכך needs its own פסוק; (3) whether the הלכה reduces or adds; (4) whether the first mention is counted. All four arrive at the same results: the רבנן require 2 full walls plus a טפח, and רבי שמעון requires 3 full walls plus a טפח.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: everyone agrees
that when the הלכה comes, it is to take away,
and that we follow the spelling.
And here they disagree about learning from first mentions:
One Sage holds: we do learn from the first mention,
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון: four walls.

phrases.english: And the other Sage holds: we do not learn from the first mention.
phrases.notes: The רבנן: three walls.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא, כִּי אֲתַאי הִלְכְתָא — לְגָרֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another alternative explanation. It keeps the 'reduce' view from step 15 and moves the argument to a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the root of the מחלוקת?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Whether the first mention of the word סוכה is counted (דורשין תחילות).

steps.title: רב מתנה brings a different source for רבי שמעון from ישעיה
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה says רבי שמעון learns from the פסוק that a סוכה protects from storm and rain. A real shelter needs three full walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: רבי שמעון's reason comes from here: "And there will be a סוכה for shade by day from the heat, and for refuge and cover from storm and from rain."
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה leaves the counting method behind. He gives a completely different reason for רבי שמעון, taken from a פסוק in ישעיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes a סוכה as protection from storm and rain. Something with only two full walls does not really shelter you. So רבי שמעון requires three full walls, and the הלכה adds a fourth wall of a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: Refuge and cover, meaning real shelter

phrases.english: רב מתנה said:
The reason of רבי שמעון is from here:
"And there will be a סוכה for shade by day from the heat,
phrases.notes: ישעיה ד:ו

phrases.english: and for refuge and cover from storm and from rain."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מַתְנָה אָמַר: טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new source for רבי שמעון that does not depend on counting words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is רבי שמעון's source for requiring three full walls?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in ישעיה: a סוכה must be a real shelter from storm and rain.

steps.title: Where is the one-טפח wall placed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the small one-טפח wall should stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that טפח, where does he stand it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks a practical question about the small wall. This sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view here is that a סוכה can have two full walls plus a third wall that is only a טפח wide. The גמרא wants to know exactly where that narrow wall must go to be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: He stands it up, or places it

phrases.english: And that handbreadth, where does he stand it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹתוֹ טֶפַח הֵיכָן מַעֲמִידוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the source of the law to how it is carried out in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where must the one-טפח wall be placed?

steps.title: רב: the טפח stands opposite the wall that sticks out
steps.stepSummary: רב says to place the טפח at the end of one full wall, facing the other full wall that comes out from the corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: He stands it opposite the one that comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question about where the small wall goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture two full walls meeting at a corner, like the letter L. The טפח-wall is placed at the open end of one full wall, facing the other full wall. This way the small wall sits next to a real wall instead of floating alone in the open space.

keyTerms.meaning: Opposite the one that comes out, meaning facing the other full wall

steps.whatToRemember: With two full walls and a טפח, the טפח goes at the end of one full wall, facing the other full wall.

phrases.english: רב said:
He stands it opposite the one that comes out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מַעֲמִידוֹ כְּנֶגֶד הַיּוֹצֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The טפח is placed at the end of one full wall, facing the other full wall.

steps.title: רב כהנא and רב אסי Turn to Question רב
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא and רב אסי begin to respond to רב's ruling about where the one-טפח wall goes. Their actual words come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא and רב אסי said to רב:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is only a setup. The גמרא is telling us that רב כהנא and רב אסי are about to challenge רב's ruling, and their challenge comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 19, רב said to put the טפח at the end of one full wall, facing the other full wall. Now his two students speak up to him. This tells us his placement is about to be tested, probably with an easier or more natural way to stand the טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: They said to him. This often opens a challenge or question to a teacher.
An אמורא, a student of רב
An אמורא, a student and colleague of רב

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here and think the line says anything about the law. It only tells you who is speaking. The real challenge comes in the next line.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to Rav:
phrases.notes: An attribution line only. It opens the students' response to רב's placement of the טפח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a response to רב's answer in Step 19 about where the one-טפח wall should stand.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the טפח is placed at the end of one full wall, facing the other full wall
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The content of the challenge appears on the next amud. Here we are only told that רב's students are about to question his placement.
